CALGARY, AB / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Jade Leader Corp, ("Jade Leader" or the "Company") announces a change of the Company's auditor. At the request of the Company, BDO Canada LLP (the "Former Auditor") has resigned as auditor of the Company effective November 26, 2026. The audit committee and board of directors of the Company have appointed Crowe MacKay LLP as the successor auditor, effective November 26, 2026 (the "Successor Auditor") and this appointment will be placed before Shareholders for approval thereto at the Corporation's next Annual General Meeting.

The Company has sent a Notice of Change of Auditor (the "Notice") to the Former Auditor and to the Successor Auditor and has received a letter from each, addressed to the securities commissions in each of Alberta, British Columbia and Ontario stating that they agree with the information contained in the Notice. The Notice together with the letter from the Former Auditor and the letter from the Successor Auditor have been reviewed and approved by the Company's board of directors and are available on the SEDAR+ website at www.sedarplus.ca.

There were no disagreements or unresolved issues between the Company and the Former Auditor on any matter of audit scope or procedures, accounting principles or policies, or financial statement disclosure. It is the Company's opinion that there have been no "reportable events" (as defined in National Instrument 51-102 - Continuous Disclosure Obligations) between the Company and the Former Auditor. The Former Auditor did not provide a modified opinion in their auditor's report for the financial statements of the Company for the fiscal years ended September 30, 2024 and September 30, 2025.

MAHIA, New Zealand, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rocket Lab Corporation (Nasdaq: RKLB), a global leader in launch services and space systems, today successfully completed another dedicated Electron launch for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite operator Synspective.

The ‘Night Owls Never Sleep’ mission launched from Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand at 1:15 p.m. NZDT on 27 September 2026, delivering the 14h StriX satellite directly into a 569km low Earth orbit. This latest addition further scales Synspective’s Earth-observation constellation that gathers high-resolution images of the planet's surface regardless of weather conditions or time of day.

Today’s mission was Rocket Lab’s 22nd launch of 2026 and 101st mission overall, extending Electron’s lead as the world’s most frequently-launched small-lift orbital rocket.

Mission Highlights:

  • Unmatched Track Record: Maintaining a 100% mission success rate for Synspective, Rocket Lab has been the sole launch provider for all 14 StriX satellites to date.
  • Rapid Constellation Building: As Rocket Lab’s 22nd mission of the year, today’s launch highlights Electron’s high-cadence reliability that commercial constellation operators depend on to scale their operations on schedule.
  • Record-Breaking Partnership: Following a historic 20-launch deal signed in September - the largest commercial contract for Electron to date - Synspective is Rocket Lab’s largest launch customer with 47 total missions booked. Today’s launch leaves 33 dedicated missions on the manifest to be launched through 2031, giving Synspective long-term certainty as they build out their constellation.

Net Revenue Up 6% in the Third Quarter; System Sales Exceed $8M in a Quarter; Company Makes Multiple Growth Investments in Q3, Including New Studio Opening and Acquisition

Boston, MA, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MiniLuxe Holding Corp. (TSXV: MNLX) today announced its financial results for the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 27, 2026 (“Q3 2026” and “YTD 2026”, respectively). The comparative prior year periods are the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 28, 2025.

MiniLuxe is on a mission to make self-care something you can feel good about, starting with your nails. The Company delivers premium nail care in studios known for hospital-grade hygiene, cleaner polishes, and treatments that are better for you and for the people who provide them. What sets MiniLuxe apart is its people and culture, which are at the center of its competitive advantage. In an industry infamous for churn and poor working conditions, MiniLuxe has retained 86% of its hourly workforce on average over each of the last three years. Team members who are with the Company five years or more receive stock options, giving them a stake in the Company’s success, along with real career paths. Today, more than half of MiniLuxe’s service professionals (nail designers and waxing specialists) have reached that milestone.

The third quarter of 2026 delivered another quarter of year-over-year growth, with total Company net revenue up 6.1% to $7.7M and system sales up 8% to $8.1M from $7.5M in Q3 2025. Growth was driven by continued same-studio sales gains in both volume and mix. System sales include sales from all MiniLuxe studios, including franchised locations. The quarter extends a long, unbroken run of year-over-year revenue growth, reflecting continued demand for MiniLuxe services.

The Company made multiple growth investments in the third quarter: new studios, new AI-driven, geo-targeted paid marketing tests, upgrades to existing studios, and additional nail designer hours ahead of the fourth-quarter holiday season, its period of peak demand. While these initiatives resulted in some short-term margin pullback, management expects them to deliver meaningful returns over the longer term. After the quarter ended, the Company also put in place its first price increase in approximately three years, of approximately 5%, which management expects to more than offset rising labor and health care benefit costs.

  • New studios: The Company opened its Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio on July 30 and acquired a majority interest in an existing studio in Burlington, Massachusetts on September 4. The third quarter was also the first full quarter for the new MiniLuxe Lakewood studio in Dallas.
  • Marketing tests: Early results are encouraging, with some test studios attracting record numbers of new clients who are also returning faster for repeat visits.
  • Studio upgrades: The Company began renovating several existing studios with new dual stations that allow a manicure and pedicure at the same time. In the first studios, these stations cost at least 50% less than legacy stations, and productivity per station has been as much as double that of legacy pedicure stations.
  • Nail designer hours: Staffed hours were up 7% over the prior year, which positions the Company well for fourth-quarter demand.

 MiniLuxe’s Focus and Key Strategic Pillars in Q3 2026

The Company continued to make meaningful progress across each of its core strategic pillars in the third quarter of fiscal 2026:

  1. Attract, develop and retain high-quality nail designer talent;
  2. Drive growth through operating partners and franchise partners;
  3. Accelerate overall studio-level profitability and drive overall Company profitability;
  4. Strengthen balance sheet with sufficient capital to execute against growth plans.

  • Total Company net revenue grew 6.1% to $7.7M in Q3 2026 from $7.3M in Q3 2025, bringing year-to-date revenue to $21.8M, up 4.3% from $20.9M in YTD 2025.

The Company continued to expand through operating partners and franchise partners. Overall gross franchise sales were up 53% in the third quarter and 102% year to date.  The Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio opened on July 30, 2026, the Lakewood (Dallas) studio reopened as a MiniLuxe studio on June 5, 2026, and the Burlington, Massachusetts studio, acquired September 4, 2026, is operated through a 51%-owned limited liability company with its existing owner as operating partner.

Management Commentary

“In Q3, we continued to grow revenue year over year and expanded our studio footprint, with new studio openings and new locations in development. We also increased total nail designer hours and put marketing tests in place to attract new customers. We are already seeing early results as we attract new customers and see repeat visits, and we believe these investments will deliver a significant return over the medium to longer term. One of the most noteworthy statistics for me is that about half of our customer base is now Gen Z, which bodes well for the longevity of our brand and customer lifetime value.” – Tony Tjan, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

Other Developments

  • Substantial Issuer Bid (SIB). The Company’s SIB for up to C$6.0 million of its Class A Subordinate Voting Shares expired at 5:00 p.m. (Toronto time) on September 24, 2026. No Subordinate Voting Shares were purchased under the offer and all tendered shares were returned to shareholders.
  • Paintbox New York studio. On September 7, 2026, the Company closed its “store-in-store” Paintbox studio in New York, New York. The Company had a short-term arrangement with a hair studio to use its space as a “store-in-store” concept, and the arrangement was not extended.
  • Acquisition of Belle Vista Nail Studio. On September 4, 2026, the Company formed MNLX Burlington JV LLC and acquired the assets of Belle Vista Nail Studio in Burlington, Massachusetts for cash consideration of approximately $0.3M, issuing a 49% interest in the new company to the sellers. MiniLuxe will convert this studio to its own brand in 2027.

The Company continues to evaluate accretive M&A opportunities and is in discussions with several nail studio operators that it believes fit its purpose of empowering nail designers, and where it can create shared value by applying MiniLuxe’s brand standards and back-office infrastructure.

Non-IFRS Measures and Reconciliation of Non-IFRS Measures

This press release references certain non-IFRS measures used by management. These measures are not recognized under International Financial Reporting Standards (“IFRS”), do not have a standardized meaning prescribed by IFRS, and are therefore unlikely to be comparable to similar measures presented by other companies. Rather, these measures are provided as additional information to complement those IFRS measures by providing further understanding of the Company’s results of operations from management’s perspective. Accordingly, these measures should not be considered in isolation nor as a substitute for analysis of the Company’s financial information reported under IFRS. The non-IFRS measures referred to in this press release are “Adjusted EBITDA”, “Normalized Adjusted EBITDA”, and system sales.

Adjusted EBITDA

Management believes Adjusted EBITDA most accurately reflects the commercial reality of the Company’s operations on an ongoing basis by adding back non-cash expenses. Additionally, the rent-related adjustments ensure that studio-related expenses align with revenue generated over the corresponding time periods.

Adjusted EBITDA is calculated by adding back fixed asset depreciation, right-of-use asset amortization under IFRS 16, asset disposal, and share-based compensation expense to IFRS operating income, then deducting cash rent expenses net of lease abatements. When relevant, we will add back adjustments made to the P&L as a result of accounting policies that are non-cash or do not have operational impacts (for example, inventory adjustments or deferred revenue). IFRS operating income is revenue less cost of sales (gross profit), additionally adjusted for general and administrative expenses, and depreciation and amortization expenses. Normalized Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA, further adjusted to (i) remove items that management considers one-time or not representative of ongoing operations, and (ii) present the comparative period on a basis consistent with the current period. Management uses Normalized Adjusted EBITDA to assess the Company’s run-rate operating performance. It should be read together with, and not as a substitute for, operating loss and Adjusted EBITDA.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - NTG Clarity Networks Inc. (TSXV: NCI) (OTC Pink: NYWKF) ("NTG" or the "Company") today reported its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All figures are in Canadian dollars.

Q3 2026 Highlights

Comparisons are to the quarter ended September 30, 2025 unless otherwise stated.

  • Revenue: was $19.2M, down 7.9% year-over-year from $20.9M and down 4.3% from $20.1M in Q2 2026. The sequential decline has narrowed in each quarter of 2026 as the situation in the middle east shows early signs of stability. Year-to-date revenue is up approximately 2% year-over-year to $60.6M compared to $59.4M in 2025.

  • Gross Profit: was $6.3M or 33.0% of revenue, compared to $7.3M or 34.9%, reflecting pricing concessions on renewals.

  • Net Income: Total comprehensive income was $0.2M or 1.0% of revenue, compared to $1.9M or 9.1%, reflecting lower operating leverage in the quarter. NTG's delivery capacity is its strongest asset and keeping it in place, as discussed in Q2, allows us to take advantage of new opportunities.

  • Adjusted EBITDA: was $0.6M or 2.9% of revenue, compared to $2.5M or 11.9% in 2025, and compared to approximately nil in Q2 2026. Revenue was $0.9M lower than in Q2 2026 and the cost base was $1.4M lower.

  • Operating Cash Flow: of $3.2M, compared to an outflow of $3.3M in Q3 2025 and an outflow of $4.6M in Q2 2026. Cash was $3.4M at September 30, 2026, compared to $2.8M at June 30, 2026.

  • Purchase Orders: $33.4M announced in Q3 2026, or 1.7 times revenue, compared to $12.3M in Q2 2026

"We are seeing early signs of stability, both in the wider Saudi economy, where GDP recovered slightly from Q2, and in purchase order activity from our clients," said Adam Zaghloul, Vice President of Strategy & Planning at NTG Clarity. "Purchase orders were $33.4 million in the third quarter and we have announced a further $24.5 million since. Our focus now is staffing those orders and turning them into billings. Collections improved in the quarter, bringing receivables and unbilled contract assets down, and that progress has continued into the fourth quarter. We have worked with our clients on pricing and billing through a difficult period, and we believe that is how long-term relationships in the Kingdom are built."

Fiscal 2026 Financial Outlook

The prolonged conflict in the Middle East has disrupted oil shipments through the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, on which many digitization initiatives in Saudi Arabia and the rest of the Gulf rely for funding. Saudi enterprises have responded with a focus on cost savings and return on investment. Some customers have negotiated more favourable pricing, paused expansion and in some cases scaled back their engagements.

Revenue declined again in Q3 as these adjustments took effect. However, order intake has been steadier, starting in Q3 and extending into the fourth quarter, with an increased pace of new purchase orders, a four-year extension of an existing framework agreement and a new three-year framework agreement with a new customer. NTG has worked with its customers through this period on pricing, on billing terms and on the size of their engagements. The Company believes that supporting its customers during these difficult conditions strengthens its standing in the region. The new framework agreement announced on November 17, 2026 marks the fourth portfolio company of one of the Kingdom's largest investment entities to become an NTG customer and is a sign of the growing position of NTG within some of the most prestigious companies in the region.

Management is continually evaluating the prospects for future growth against its delivery capacity with an eye towards cash generation and improving profitability. NTG's top priority is cash collections and receivables management so that it remains self-funded during the turbulence in the Middle East. Q3 showed progress, with an overall reduction in accounts receivable due to strong collections and no bad debts expected. Those collections continued into Q4, which showed receivables decreasing by approximately a further $4M by the end of October.

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

NTG references Adjusted EBITDA, which is a non-IFRS (non-GAAP) measure and Adjusted EBITDA margin, which is a non-GAAP ratio. Adjusted EBITDA means adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization. EBITDA is equal to net income (loss) before income taxes plus finance costs plus depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is equal to EBITDA before other discretionary expenses and expenses outside of the control of NTG. In NTG's case these are other income, share-based payments, and expenses related to foreign exchange. Adjusted EBITDA margin is Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue.

Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin are not recognized measures under IFRS. Delta, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Fab-Form Industries Ltd. (TSXV: FBF) ("Fab-Form®", or the "Company") is pleased to announce that the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO") has allowed the patent claims for its innovative SPACE-R product. This allowance represents a significant milestone in the Company's ongoing commitment to innovation, product development and delivering advanced solutions to contractors worldwide. The patent is expected to be formally issued in due course.

SPACE-R addresses three challenges in creating reinforced concrete columns. First, it replaces the traditional horizontal steel stirrup with a lightweight fiberglass component, significantly reducing shipping costs and eliminating corrosion issues. Second, it utilizes polypropylene clips to connect vertical rebar to the horizontal stirrup, reducing onsite labor and eliminating human error. Thirdly, it features polypropylene fins on the outside to ensure the reinforcement is correctly positioned within the column form, a task typically accomplished with rebar wheels in the industry. 

ABSTRACT OF THE DISCLOSURE
There is provided a formwork assembly. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of longitudinally-extending and laterally spaced-apart steel reinforcing bars. The formwork assembly includes a hoop reinforcement shaped to extend about the reinforcing bars. The hoop reinforcement is configured to provide shear strength to concrete poured into the formwork so positioned. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of receptacles circumferentially spaced-apart about, coupled to and radially inwardly-extending from the hoop reinforcement so as to promote a desired positioning or spacing of the reinforcing bars. The formwork assembly includes a plurality of spacers circumferentially spaced-apart about, coupled to and radially outwardly-extending from the hoop reinforcement. The formwork assembly includes a formwork shaped to extend about and be positioned in place via the plurality of spacers. There is further provided a concrete stirrup apparatus comprising said hoop reinforcement, receptacles and spacers.

Delta, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Fab-Form Industries Ltd. (TSXV: FBF) ("Fab-Form" or the "Company") announced today its financial results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, the first quarter of fiscal 2027. All amounts are in Canadian dollars unless otherwise stated.

Financial Highlights

Against the backdrop of a soft Canadian construction market and the Company's first quarter of direct operations in Missouri, the Company reports:

  • Revenue for the first quarter decreased 7.52% to $1,367,898 compared to $1,479,187 in the quarter ended 30 September 2025, mainly due to declines in Nudura Insulated Concrete Forms ("ICF") sales (-18.71%), the Company's largest product line, Helix (-85.83%), ICF accessories (-69.96%) and Monopour (-14.36%). The decrease was partially offset by growth in Bracing (+51.73%), Fast-Tube® (+94.07%) and Fastfoot® (+16.37%) sales. The growth in Bracing and Fastfoot® was mainly due to the establishment of the Company's Missouri operations.

  • Gross profit increased 2.11% to $533,349 from $522,333, and gross margin improved to 39.0% from 35.3%. Cost of sales fell 12.78%, faster than revenue, reflecting a shift in sales mix towards higher margin products, lower sales of low margin products and the contribution from Missouri.

  • Operating expenses increased 15.57% to $290,980. General and administrative expenses rose 28.77% to $233,319, mainly due to higher wages and benefits (+40.09%) and research and development expenses (+84.57%), while selling and marketing expenses fell 18.31% to $57,661.

  • Earnings from operations declined 10.42% to $242,369, compared to $270,553 in the same quarter last year. Operating margin was 17.7% compared to 18.3%.

  • Other income fell 95.20% to $2,246, compared to $46,840 in the same quarter last year, following the retirement of a short-term investment to acquire property in White Rock.

  • Net earnings for the quarter were $179,945 ($0.020 per share), down 24.21% from $237,434 ($0.026 per share) in the same quarter last year.

Financial Position

  • As of 30 September 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $1,788,621, up $193,280 (12.1%) from $1,595,341 at 30 June 2026 and up $451,912 (33.8%) from $1,336,709 at 30 September 2025.

  • Net cash generated from operating activities was $329,548 (2025: $362,982). Cash of $123,932 was used in investing activities, comprising property and equipment ($17,391), product development ($47,001) and intangible assets ($59,540). Cash of $30,566 was used in financing activities for lease payments on the Delta, BC office and warehouses.

  • Total assets grew to $7,844,954 from $7,436,824 at 30 June 2026, and shareholders' equity increased to $6,497,998 from $6,318,053.

  • The Company has no long-term debt other than lease liabilities, with total liabilities of $1,346,956, ensuring financial stability and flexibility for future growth.

Product and Market Update

Fab-Form continues to focus on its core product lines while advancing innovative solutions in concrete forming technology. Highlights for the quarter include:

U.S. Expansion - Missouri Branch

The Missouri branch generated revenue of $306,003 in its first quarter of operations, representing 22.4% of Company revenue. Its gross profit was $186,050, a gross margin of 60.8%, and it contributed 34.9% of Company gross profit. The decision to operate directly in Missouri responds to U.S. tariffs, the need for shorter delivery times for U.S. customers and a soft Canadian construction market. Tariffs are now paid only on steel costs rather than on selling prices, reducing the Company's exposure. Tariffs are expected to remain a challenge for steel exports to the U.S., and any further changes could affect steel product sales growth.

The Missouri location provides quick access to all U.S. states, supports distributors and contractors, and ties into the Company's target of US$3 million in additional revenue within 24 months. It also provides a base to introduce Fast-Tube® 3.0, Space-R™, Flex-R™, Ever-Wall™ and Zuckle™ 2XK into the U.S. market.

Fast-Tube®

Fast-Tube® sales almost doubled, rising 94.07% to $82,224. In late September, a record test pour was completed at the Company's Springfield, Missouri warehouse, in which a 40-foot Fast-Tube® column was poured in just 70 minutes, a speed the Company believes no other forming system can match, and which demonstrates the pouring advantages Fast-Tube® offers contractors over cardboard tubes.

New Patent Applications and Zuckle™ 2XK

During the quarter the Company applied for two new patents, Ever-Wall™ and Zuckle 2XK™.

The Company also completed the design and specification of the new version of its drill adjustable wall aligner, Zuckle 2XK. Production of the first batch began shortly after quarter end, and the product is expected to be available to customers in mid-February 2027 from both the Delta, BC and Missouri locations. Recent test profiles show a load capacity approaching 13,000 lb, and the product has been engineered for low-cost production.

CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TC Energy Corporation (TSX, NYSE: TRP) (TC Energy or the Company) today announced the closing of an agreement with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership (CGL FNLP), an Indigenous-led investment entity representing 12 First Nations along the Coastal GasLink (CGL) corridor, including Cheslatta Carrier Nation; Kitselas First Nation; Lheidli T’enneh First Nation; Nadleh Whut’en First Nation, Nee Tahi Buhn Indian Band; Saik’uz First Nation; Skin Tyee Nation; Stellat'en First Nation; Ts’il Kaz Koh First Nation; Wet’suwet’en First Nation; Witset First Nation; and Yekooche First Nation.

Through the agreement, participating Nations have acquired an economic interest in the entity that holds TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL. These communities are expected to benefit from long-term predictable financial returns associated with TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL.

This transaction marks the second Indigenous investment involving TC Energy's interest in CGL and reflects years of partnership with Indigenous communities along the corridor.

Creating opportunities through partnership
“This transaction demonstrates what is possible when Indigenous communities, industry and governments come together with a shared commitment to creating opportunities that deliver benefits over the long term,” said François Poirier, President and Chief Executive Officer of TC Energy. “It reflects the strength of the relationships developed along the Coastal GasLink corridor over more than a decade of collaboration and our shared belief that major projects should create lasting value for the communities connected to them.”

“This investment represents a historic milestone for our Nations and a new chapter in our relationship with Coastal GasLink,” said Corrina Leween, Director & Executive Committee member, CGL FNLP. “It reflects years of work to advance Indigenous participation in major infrastructure projects and to create a stronger role for our Nations in shaping the economic future of our territories. Through this transaction, our Nations will benefit from a long-term economic interest that provides stable, predictable returns for our communities, helping support future generations and strengthen our collective prosperity. Today’s achievement would not have been possible without the vision and leadership of the late Niilo Edwards, whose commitment to Indigenous economic empowerment helped bring our Nations together around this opportunity.”

Expanding pathways to participation
This transaction was supported by a loan guarantee made available under the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program, administered by the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation (CILGC).

“We commend TC Energy for working with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership to advance this investment. Partnerships like this can support a more inclusive approach to infrastructure development while strengthening Indigenous economic self-determination and creating opportunities for Nations to share in long-term, project benefits,” said Kristan Straub, President and CEO, Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation.

“At a time when Canada must build big things again, in partnership with Indigenous Peoples, projects like Coastal GasLink are helping us strengthen our economic sovereignty, diversify our trade, advance reconciliation and Indigenous prosperity, and secure our place as a global energy superpower. By combining Indigenous economic participation with the investment certainty needed to advance major projects, we are responsibly driving Canada's next generation of growth,” said the Honourable Tim Hodgson, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.

“Economic reconciliation is about ensuring that Indigenous communities have the opportunity to own, invest in, and benefit from the major projects shaping Canada’s future. This investment will support 12 First Nations in acquiring an interest in, and derive meaningful long-term benefits from, one of Canada’s most important energy infrastructure projects. By helping unlock Indigenous ownership in major projects, we are creating opportunities to build long-term wealth, generate sustainable revenues, and advance economic self-determination for generations to come,” said the Honourable François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue.

Building on more than a decade of partnership
For many participating Nations, this agreement represents the next chapter in a relationship with CGL that spans more than a decade.

The investment opportunity was made available to all 20 Indigenous communities with existing CGL agreements. Participation reflects the independent decisions of each Nation based on its own priorities and objectives.

On Oct. 13, 2026, TC Energy announced its first Indigenous investment agreement related to CGL, involving participating Nations represented through FN CGL Pipeline Limited Partnership. Together, the two agreements build on years of partnership and create additional opportunities for Indigenous communities to benefit from the long-term financial returns associated with TC Energy's limited partner interest in CGL.

A critical pathway for Canadian LNG exports
As operator and co-owner of CGL, TC Energy safely delivers 2.1 billion cubic feet per day of Canadian natural gas to LNG Canada in Kitimat, B.C., supporting Canadian LNG exports to global markets. With the announcement of CGL Phase 2, system capacity will nearly double, demonstrating the growing global demand for natural gas and long-term value of Canadian LNG exports.

Transaction advisors
RBC Capital Markets acted as financial advisor to TC Energy and Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP as legal counsel.

For CGL First Nations Limited Partnership, National Bank of Canada Capital Markets acted as business and financial advisors, and Gowling WLG acted as legal counsel.

About TC Energy
We are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets—powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America. 

We carry forward a legacy of nation building energy infrastructure and strong partnerships. By working with communities, businesses and leaders across our extensive energy network, we create opportunities today and for generations to come. 

TC Energy’s common shares trade on the Toronto (TSX) and New York (NYSE) stock exchanges under the symbol TRP. To learn more, visit us at TCEnergy.com.

About Coastal GasLink
CGL is Canada’s first direct pathway to global LNG export markets. It is a 670-kilometre (416-mile) natural gas pipeline that safely delivers 2.1 Bcf/d of natural gas from northeastern British Columbia to the LNG Canada facility in Kitimat, B.C., where it is liquefied for export to global markets. The infrastructure is owned by Coastal GasLink Pipeline Limited Partnership, with TC Energy as the operator.

About CGL First Nations Limited Partnership
CGL First Nations Limited Partnership comprises of 12 First Nations that will collectively hold an economic interest in the entity holding TC Energy’s limited partner interest in the Coastal GasLink project. The partnership was established to pursue collective economic opportunities and advance Indigenous ownership in the Coastal GasLink project, creating long-term benefits for participating Nations and future generations.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / LUNR Aerospace Corp. (CSE:FLY)(Frankfurt:6GB)(WKN:A4269V) is pleased to announce the appointment of Mr. Cameron Chell to its Board of Directors (the "Board"). Mr. Chell is the President, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Draganfly Inc. (NASDAQ:DPRO), a developer of drone systems and autonomous technologies. With more than 30 years of entrepreneurial and executive experience, Mr. Chell brings an extensive background in establishing, financing and growing technology companies across aerospace, defence, autonomous systems, advanced manufacturing and public markets.1

Mr. Chell has founded and co-founded numerous technology ventures, including Engyro, an enterprise software company whose technology was acquired by Microsoft Corporation in 2007.2 He also founded FutureLink, an early developer and operator of data centres for the provision of internet-based software applications including the first to deploy enterprise level applications as the precursor to modern cloud computing services.

His experience in the aerospace sector includes co-founding UrtheCast Corp., a Canadian Earth-observation technology company that developed and deployed high-definition imaging systems on the outside of the International Space Station ("ISS"). In 2015, UrtheCast released what it described as the world's first full-colour HD videos of Earth captured from the ISS.3 The company subsequently ranked first in Deloitte's 2016 Technology Fast 50 program, recognizing it as Canada's fastest-growing technology company based on revenue growth between 2012 and 2015.4

In his current leadership roles at Draganfly, Mr. Chell oversees the publicly traded company developing unmanned aircraft systems and related technologies for commercial, public safety and defence applications. In September 2026, Draganfly announced that it had been awarded a five-year contract by the Government of Canada to supply tactical intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance drone systems to the Canadian Armed Forces.5

Mr. Chell's broader business experience also includes serving as co-founder and chairman of KODAKOne, a digital image rights management platform developed in conjunction with the Eastman Kodak Company.6 His entrepreneurial career has attracted international media attention, including Forbes7 plus television appearances involving CNN8, Fox Business9 and the RedChip Money Report on Bloomberg Television10. He has also been a featured speaker at events at the United Nations, TEDx Montréal Women, and has opened for Tony Robbins on multiple occasions sharing perspectives on entrepreneurship, technology and leadership.11

"I am pleased to join LUNR Aerospace's Board of Directors at an important stage in the Company's development. With the growing importance of sovereign space access for national security, defence and commercial applications, I believe LUNR is pursuing a significant opportunity, but more importantly, a critical mission to help establish Canadian orbital launch capabilities and address the increasing global demand for secure, reliable and cost-effective access to space. I look forward to working with the entire LUNR team to advance the Company's strategic objectives in support of Canada's critical space requirements," said Cameron Chell.

"Cameron brings extensive experience in building and leading technology businesses across aerospace, defence and autonomous systems. His proven background in commercializing emerging technologies, developing strategic relationships and navigating public markets will be a valuable asset to LUNR as we advance our propulsion technologies and orbital launch capabilities. We look forward to leveraging his experience and perspective as we execute our long-term growth strategy," stated Jeanue Chung, CEO of LUNR Aerospace Corp.

About LUNR Aerospace Corp.

LUNR Aerospace Corp. is a Canadian-based company developing orbital launch capability in Canada to support sovereign access to space and serve the global launch market. The Company is focused on advancing Canadian launch infrastructure designed to help address constrained global launch capacity and enable future payload launches from Canadian soil. LUNR's planned launch systems are being designed for low-Earth orbit, polar, and sun-synchronous missions, with an emphasis on scalable vehicle architecture, reusability, and cost-efficient deployment.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - BQE Water Inc. (TSXV: BQE), a leader in the treatment and management of mine impacted waters, is pleased to release its interim consolidated financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

"With GAAP revenue up 32%, net income up 33% and Adjusted EBITDA up 38% over Q3 2025, our strong third quarter results allowed us to us to substantially narrow the gap on a year-to-date basis relative to the same period in 2025. In the third quarter, we remobilized our operations team back to the Kemess Mine, successfully restarting the treatment plant and operating it on a seasonal basis. We also initiated 3-year operations support for cyanide destruction for a facility in Alaska." said David Kratochvil, President & CEO of BQE Water. "We now have 26 treatment facilities across 11 operation sites in our recurring revenue portfolio. This growing operational base is supported by a strong pipeline of projects and opportunities that we expect to build on in the quarters ahead. In addition, we have good visibility into new near-term operating opportunities that are expected to allow us to redeploy our seasonal operations teams during the winter shutdown."

FINANCIAL HIGHLIGHTS

  • Revenues under GAAP of $12.3 million in Q3 2026, a record high for a 3-month period, compared to $9.3 million in Q3 2025, a 32% increase.

  • Proportional Revenues of $14.5 million in Q3 2026 compared to $10.7 million in Q3 2025, a 36% increase.

  • Gross margin of $5.9 million in Q3 2026 compared to $4.7 million in Q3 2025, a 25% increase.

  • Net income of $3.7 million in Q3 2026 compared to net income of $2.8 million in Q3 2025, a 33% increase.

  • Earnings per share (basic) of $2.84 in Q3 2026 compared to $2.15 in Q3 2025, a 32% increase.

  • Adjusted EBITDA of $4.6 million in Q3 2026 compared to $3.3 million in Q3 2025, a 38% increase.

  • Working capital of $25.1 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $21.4 million at December 31, 2025, a 17% increase.

COMMENTARY AND OUTLOOK
We are pleased to have delivered strong third quarter results, with GAAP revenue up 32%, proportional revenue up 36%, net income up 33% and adjusted EBITDA up 38% over Q3 2025. In line with our previously communicated expectations, our strong third quarter results allowed us to us to substantially narrow the gap on a year-to-date basis relative to the same period in 2025.

Matching last year's Proportional Revenue on a year-to-date basis masks the strong underlying growth in our business. Recall that 2025 included a one-time revenue contract for the equipment sale, construction, design and commissioning of the Valley Tailings Facility, which was all recorded under technical services (advisory and design) revenue. Excluding the equipment sale component of $4.6 million from 2025, our year-to-date GAAP revenue increased 13% year-over-year, while our share of revenues from joint ventures in China also grew 38%. Although we are not eliminating the possibility of future equipment sales, the Company's business model is based on professional services linked to clean water production and our strategic focus is on our ability to grow our delivery of services, not equipment.

The primary driver of our growth in Q3 2026 and year-to-date has been recurring operations and short-term operations, which accounted for 81% and 77% of our Q3 2026 and year-to-date GAAP revenue, up from 67% and 59% in the comparable 2025 periods. In 2026, the Company operated a portfolio of 26 treatment facilities across 11 operation sites. On a year-to-date basis, new operations and support services contributed $4.6 million in additional revenue when compared to the same period in 2025. With respect to short-term operations, we added two facilities in 2026, while continuing temporary treatment at Eagle Mine. The Kemess treatment plant was recommissioned and operated for a few months in 2026, and, after a one-year hiatus, we also resumed operations at Minto Mine under a new arrangement with the new property owner, Selkirk Copper.

Excluding the above-noted equipment sale, our technical advisory and engineering services revenue has also grown but not to the same degree as our operations. We expect these services to increase gradually in Q4 2026 and into the first half of 2027 as our engineers currently undergoing site-based training to join our technical teams. All engineers hired in 2026 have been assigned to our operating sites for hands-on training before transitioning into technical teams in process design, field commissioning, or technology development. This approach is integral to the Company's vision of ensuring our technical staff develops practical field experience as a foundation for their professional growth.

Our year-to-date gross margin in dollar terms remained largely consistent at approximately $11.3 million (43.0%) compared to $11.6 million (41.4%) in the comparable prior period. The 33% decrease in year-to-date net income primarily reflects our continued investment in the people and systems required to support the Company's growth. In Q3 2026, our G&A expenses also included a one-time professional fee associated with the preparation and submission of SR&ED claims related to the Company's intellectual property and technology development activities in 2024, through which we generated $745,000 in non-refundable SR&ED investment tax credits that may be applied against future corporate income taxes payable. Moreover, under recently expanded federal and provincial SR&ED programs, the Company expects future qualifying claims for 2025 and beyond to generate refundable tax credits, providing a potential source of cash recoveries.

Our balance sheet remains strong, with working capital of $25.1 million at the end of Q3 2026, up $3.7 million from December 31, 2025. Our cash and cash equivalents stood at $17.6 million, down $1.3 million over this period, largely due to an increase in accounts receivable at the end of Q3 2026. In support of our future growth, we also invested $724,000 in capital assets during 2026, including mobile equipment at Britannia, leasehold improvements and laboratory equipment for the aquatic toxicology lab, as well as computer hardware and office equipment.

We continue to have long pipeline of projects and operations to build on the quarters ahead. While certain operations are seasonal and will pause over the winter, we have good visibility into new near-term operating opportunities that are expected to enable us to redeploy operation teams and continue generating operations revenue through the winter months. We also expect to commence several feasibility studies and a significant engineering design-for-construction project in the coming months, with anticipated project durations ranging from five to ten months.

Our growing pipeline provides strong visibility over the next 18 months. Our ability to execute on these opportunities will increasingly depend on expanding and successfully onboarding our technical team members. We will also continue to invest in and implement internal systems for accounting, safety management, and resource management to support a growing organization, resulting in additional near-term expenses. With mining industry activity remaining strong, we see a healthy environment for continued growth. We nevertheless remain mindful of geopolitical and market uncertainties and will maintain a disciplined approach to hiring, investment, and resource allocation to support profitable growth.

The Company, with our Inuit partner Nuvumiut Development, operates four water treatment plants at Raglan Mine for Glencore Canada Corporation ("Glencore"). The plants at Raglan Mine are usually shut down in the first quarter as water stored in the outdoor reservoirs is frozen. During Q3 2026, we continued treating water across all four plants for our 23rd operating season at the mine.

In 2021, we began providing operation support to two SART (sulphidization-acidification-recycling-thickening) plants at metallurgical facilities in Shandong province, China. In 2025, we commissioned the third SART plant in the same region. All three SART plants have been under our technical supervision since the start of production. During Q3 2026, our team provided ongoing technical supervision at two of the three plants as the Shandong Gold plant was shut down.

In 2022, we began operations of a treatment plant utilizing our Selen-IX™ process to remove selenium from ash pond water for WesTech Engineering ("WesTech"). In Q3 2026, our team continued on site, providing water treatment services with the Selen-IX™ circuit to manage the presence of selenium in the feed.

In 2022, we began operations of a treatment plant utilizing a combination of nanofiltration and our proprietary selenium electroreduction process for the simultaneous removal of selenium and sulphate from mine water for a base metal project in the American Southwest. In 2023, our team began operations for a second newly constructed selenium removal water treatment plant at the same site. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide onsite operations support and technical supervision at both treatment plants.

In October 2025, we completed the commissioning of a Selen-IX™ treatment plant located at the Coeur Wharf Mine in South Dakota and began providing routine operation support. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide onsite and offsite support to the selenium removal circuit to manage the presence of selenium in the feed.

In January 2026, we assumed operational responsibility for the provision of operations and maintenance services for the Britannia Mine water treatment plant for the BC government under a 20-year arrangement. This High-Density Sludge lime treatment plant neutralizes acidity and removes heavy metals, primarily copper and zinc, from the mine water collected in the legacy underground workings prior to its discharge into Howe Sound. In Q3 2026, our team continued to operate and treat water daily without interruption until August 2026 and carried out the annual shut-down maintenance in September 2026.

In February 2026, we initiated an annual operation support arrangement with an integrated lead smelter-recycling facility in Eastern Canada. Prior to this arrangement, we completed an upgrade to the existing treatment system, implemented a new sulphate removal stage to a discharge limit of less than 1,500 mg/L and provided short-term operations support for the newly upgraded facility. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide ongoing site support and technical supervision.

In May 2026, we initiated a 3-year water treatment operations contract, with our Inuit partner Nuvumiut Development, to operate five treatment systems at the Nunavik Nickel Project owned by Canadian Royalties Inc. Treatment operations typically run from May to October depending on the volume of water requiring treatment. In Q3 2026, the operations team continued to operate across all five treatment systems.

In August 2026, we initiated a 3-year operations support contract to optimize a cyanide destruction circuit for a metallurgical facility in Alaska, USA. The support is intended to achieve consistent cyanide destruction performance, reducing reagent consumption, minimizing dilution water requirements, improving operational consistency between shifts, and ensuring effective implementation of the operating strategies and control philosophy. In Q3 2026, we mobilized our support team to support the facility.

SHORT-TERM OPERATIONS SERVICES HIGHLIGHTS
In addition to long-term operations, BQE Water provides operations and technical support services on a temporary basis at several sites. Short-term operations are non-recurring in nature with contracts typically lasting less than a year. Short-term operations during Q3 2026 are summarized below.

  • Continued providing water treatment operations services for the temporary emergency treatment system at the Eagle Gold Mine in the Yukon.

  • Continued operations at the ERDC Valley Tailings facility in the Yukon, which was constructed and commissioned last year.

  • Continued providing operations services at Minto Mine in the Yukon.

  • Initiated operations at the Kemess Mine water treatment plant in BC, which was the first selenium removal plant commissioned in 2020.

  • Demobilized our team from site services at Bell Mine in BC.

TECHNICAL SERVICES HIGHLIGHTS
BQE Water's technical expertise and IP are applicable globally across broad areas of water management. Highlights of some of our technical services and technical innovation projects during Q3 2026 are summarized below.

Trusted Advisory Services (Water Management and Water Studies)

  • Continued providing water management and treatment design advisory services to an operating mine in Ontario.

  • Completed lab testing and issued a report for ammonia management to a mining operation in Saskatchewan.

  • Continued to provide water management and treatment design advisory services to the KSM project in BC.

  • Continued providing water management and treatment design advisory services to a new mine undergoing permitting in the Yukon.

  • Initiated laboratory testing and advisory services to a new project in prefeasibility stage in Argentina.

  • Continued with detailed engineering for a water treatment system using ion exchange to expand rhenium production at an existing facility in Eastern Canada.

  • Continued to provide engineering design services for a water treatment system integrated into a rare earth extraction project in Brazil.

  • Performed a study to identify options for implementing selenium removal at an operating site in Quebec.

  • Completed engineering advisory services and restarted the selenium removal plant for short-term operations for the Kemess project in BC.

  • Completed a review of water treatment proposed for a new mine undergoing permitting in Yukon on behalf of the Yukon Government.

  • Initiated a pre-feasibility study engineering design for a plant to selectively recovery cobalt and scandium from copper heap leach solution in Chile.

  • Performed a review and assessment of opportunities to improve mine water treatment systems operations at legacy mines in Greece.

  • Performed a field assessment of selenium mitigation at a mine in Europe including a plan for implementing active treatment in the next 18 months.

Cyanide Management (Destruction and Recycle)

  • Completed engineering advisory services for cyanide destruction for a project in Australia.

  • Completed SART design for a new heap leach project in Mexico.

  • Continued providing engineering advisory services for estimating cyanide emissions, designing an emissions control system for cyanide, and revising engineering design of cyanide destruction for a project in the US.

  • Continued to provide plant engineering design services requiring an end-of-pipe cyanide level below 8 ppb to a project in the US.

  • Initiated field engineering advisory services for improving cyanide destruction performance at a mine in Alaska.

  • Continued detailed engineering for SART integration into the New Britannia mill in Manitoba, Canada.

Aquatic Toxicology Services

  • Continued assessment of chronic effects on aquatic environment caused by mine effluent at a mine in Western Canada.

  • Continued investigation into the effects of ammonia on acute toxicity under site-specific conditions at a mine in Eastern Canada.

  • Continued routine effluent toxicity quality monitoring for Eagle Mine water treatment operations and investigated the root cause of algae bloom.

  • Initiated laboratory tests required to establish a site-specific performance objective limit for sulphate and total dissolved solids at a mine in BC.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / North Shore Uranium Ltd. (TSXV:NSU)(OTCQB:NSURF) ("North Shore" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has closed its non-brokered private placement offering previously announced on November 18, 2026 (the "Offering") for gross proceeds of $1,110,930 through the issuance of 5,847,000 flow-through common shares of the Company (each, a "FT Share"). The Offering was upsized from the previously announced maximum of $1,100,000.

Each FT Share was issued at a price of $0.19 per FT Share. Each FT Share was issued as a "flow-through share" within the meaning of the Income Tax Act (Canada) (the "ITA").

The Company intends to use the gross proceeds of the Offering to incur "Canadian exploration expenses" that qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" (as such terms are defined in the ITA) on the Company's uranium properties in Saskatchewan, which will be renounced to the subscribers of FT Shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The costs of the Offering will be paid from the Company's general working capital.

In connection with the Offering, the Company paid cash finder's fees of $66,655.80 and issued 350,820 non-transferable finder's warrants to certain arm's length finders. Each non-transferable finder's warrant is exercisable to acquire one common share of the Company at a price of $0.19 per share for a period of two years from the date of closing the Offering, subject to compliance with the policies of the TSX Venture Exchange (the "Exchange") and applicable securities laws.

All securities issued in connection with the Offering are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 27, 2027.

The Offering remains subject to final acceptance of the Exchange.

ABOUT NORTH SHORE

The nuclear power industry is undergoing increased development to meet CO₂ emission-reduction goals and the needs of new power-intensive technologies like AI. In this environment, discoveries of uranium deposits may be significant, especially in established uranium-producing jurisdictions like New Mexico and Saskatchewan. North Shore is focused on advancing exploration for uranium deposits at Rio Puerco in the Grants Uranium District of New Mexico and its Falcon and West Bear properties at the eastern margin of the Athabasca Basin in Saskatchewan. In addition, the Company continues to evaluate quality opportunities in the United States and Canada that would complement its portfolio of uranium properties.
